events.title: Canadian Market Remains Firmly Up In Positive Territory
events.description:
The Canadian market is up firmly in positive territory around noon on Friday thanks to weak oil prices and lower bond yields aiding sentiment.

Additionally, weaker than expected jobs data from the U.S. has somewhat reduced the likelihood of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates at its next meeting later this month.

events.title: U.S. Factory Orders Inch Up In Line With Estimates In August
events.description: A report released by the Commerce Department on Friday showed a slight uptick in new orders for U.S. manufactured goods in the month of August. The Commerce Department said factory orders crept up by 0.1 percent in August after climbing by a downwardly revised 0.8 percent in July.

events.title: U.S. Employment Rises By 29,000 Jobs In September, Much Less Than Expected
events.description: The Labor Department released a closely watched report on Friday showing employment in the U.S. increased by much less than expected in the month of September. The report said non-farm payroll employment rose by 29,000 jobs in September after jumping by a downwardly revised 133,000 jobs in August. Economists had expected employment to increase by 85,000 jobs.

events.title: Euro Slides Against Majors
events.description: The euro weakened against other major currencies in the European session on Friday.

events.title: Walmart Recalls Over 4.4 Mln Grill Brushes For Ingestion Risk
events.description: Retail giant Walmart Inc. is recalling around 4.478 million units of metal wire bristle grill brushes, citing risk of ingestion and internal injuries, according to the U.S. Consumer Product safety Commission or CPSC. The recall involves certain Walmart Expert Grill brushes with black plastic or stainless-steel handles. Some brushes come with metal scraper attached.

events.title: Bay Street Headed For Positive Start
events.description:
Canadian stocks look headed for a positive start on Friday with concerns about inflation and interest rates easing a bit following a sharp drop in oil prices. Bond yields have dropped as well.

U.S. non-farm payroll data for the month of September is likely to make an impact on investor sentiment.

events.title: Swiss Franc Rises Amid Global Bonds Sell Off
events.description: The Swiss franc strengthened against other major currencies in the pre-European session on Friday, with rising government debt among the world's top nations and strong fiscal position of Switzerland.

events.title: U.S. Employment Rises Much Less Than Expected In September
events.description: The Labor Department released a closely watched report on Friday showing employment in the U.S. increased by much less than expected in the month of September.

events.title: FTSE 100 Edges Higher As Oil Prices Slip; Miners Among Top Gainers
events.description: U.K. stocks climbed higher on Friday, recovering from four successive days of decline, as weak oil prices and easing bond yields helped lift sentiment. Miners gained in strength, contributing notably to market's upmove.

events.title: Eurozone Inflation Rises To 3-Year High
events.description: Eurozone inflation accelerated more than expected to a three-year high in September on energy prices, flash estimate from Eurostat showed Friday. Inflation rose to 3.8 percent in September, marking the highest since September 2023, from 3.2 percent in August. The rate was forecast to climb to 3.7 percent.

events.title: CAC 40 Moderately Higher As Oil's Drop Lifts Sentiment
events.description: French equities gained ground Friday with the CAC 40 rising 0.69% to 7,889.67, supported by falling oil prices. Eurozone inflation accelerated to 3.8% in September versus 3.2% in August, exceeding forecasts of 3.7%.

events.title: DAX Up Firmly As Oil Prices, Bond Yields Drop
Gold Edges Up Ahead Of US Jobs Report
events.description: Gold edged up slightly on Friday as wild volatility in bond and currency markets eased ahead of the all-important U.S. jobs report due later in the day.
